title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The base is S over Z[1/2]. J is an étale degree-3 'cyclic' cover of S, the model for the three non-zero 2-torsion points; the next page calls it a torsor under (Z/3Z)_S. Σ_J = P(V_J) is a twisted P^1 with three marked sections ε_i, and Σ*_J is their complement, a twisted Legendre λ-line. t is a section of Σ*_J/S.

Previous page. Elliptic curves E/S with 2-torsion identified with J and with invariant t are equivalent to pairs (T, ν): T is an invertible module (playing T_{E,0}, the tangent line at the origin) and ν: T^{⊗2} ≃ T_{Σ,t} identifies its square with the tangent line of Σ at t. Fixing one such T_0, all others are T_0 ∧^{μ_2} E for μ_2-torsors E; these are the quadratic twists. The natural choice is T_0 = O_Σ(1)(t)^♮. But canonically T_0^{⊗2} ≃ T_{Σ,t} ∧ (μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J), so a 'reasonable' isomorphism needs a trivialization α: μ_4^♮ ≃ ω_J.

This page.
1. Once α is fixed, one gets an isomorphism κ_α: T_0^{⊗2} ≃ T_{Σ,t}. Hence one gets a canonical elliptic curve E_α attached to (J, t). Grothendieck calls it 'the universal one'. It carries a Legendre épi-structure (pinning) 'subordinate to α', since T_{E_α,0} ≃ T_0.
2. For any E over S with the same (J, t), the Legendre pinnings subordinate to α form a μ_2-torsor L_α(E).
3. Formula (57) gives an isomorphism of μ_2-torsors Isom_{S,J}(E_α, E) ≃ L_α(E), sending u to u(κ_α). The subscript J means isomorphisms compatible with J ≃_2 E ≃_2 E_α.
4. Alternatively, a section ω of ω_J itself would give a canonical E_ω with a 'naive' Legendre pinning, i.e. an isomorphism T_{E,0} ≃ O(1)(t) satisfying some condition. The next page says the two viewpoints agree once a primitive 4th root of unity i is fixed, i.e. over Z[1/2, i].

Modern reading. This is a coordinate-free, S_3-equivariant form of the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism for the Legendre family, ω_E^{⊗-2} ≅ T(λ-line). Equivalently, it says the moduli stack of elliptic curves with level-2 structure over Z[1/2] is the μ_2-gerbe of square roots of the (twisted) tangent bundle of the λ-line. The −1 automorphism and quadratic twists account for the μ_2. The Legendre pinning is a rigidification killing this gerbe. Grothendieck tracks precisely the μ_4/ω_J twist that obstructs a canonical trivialization when S_3 acts on the three 2-torsion points.
errors: 'Une fois [?]' should almost certainly read 'Une fois α fixé'.

ω_J is not defined on this page. Its precise meaning (a line attached to the Z/3-torsor J) must be taken from earlier pages, so the claim that μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J measures the obstruction is only checkable in context.

ideas.what: Elliptic curves with level-2 structure and given λ ↔ invertible T with T^{⊗2} ≃ T_{Σ,t}; twists form μ_2-torsors
ideas.modern_name: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1(log) on X(2); M(2) as a μ_2-gerbe of square roots over the λ-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kodaira–Spencer (deformation theory); Katz–Mazur and Deligne–Rapoport for the modular-curve form

ideas.what: Legendre épi-structure subordinate to α; the universal curve E_α; the torsor isomorphism Isom_{S,J}(E_α, E) ≃ L_α(E)
ideas.modern_name: Rigidification of the level-2 moduli stack by a Legendre pinning; Legendre family as a universal object after rigidification

ideas.what: Canonical twist μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J obstructing an S_3-equivariant Legendre normalization; it becomes trivial over Z[1/2, i]
ideas.modern_name: Descent of the Legendre family to M_{1,1}[1/2]; the role of μ_4 / the 4th roots of unity in the S_3 action on λ

missed.claim: A fully intrinsic, base-change-compatible description of M_{1,1} over Z[1/2]. It is built from an étale cubic J, a point t of the twisted λ-line, and a square root of its tangent line twisted by μ_4^♮ ∧ ω_J. Grothendieck explicitly isolates the μ_4 twist that obstructs a canonical Legendre normalization. This is a careful equivariant packaging rather than a new theorem.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a clean model of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a gerbe over a twisted P^1 minus 3 points. This is relevant to the arithmetic of X(2), dessins d'enfants and Galois actions on the Legendre family. However, the content is largely known through Kodaira–Spencer and level-structure theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful, coordinate-free bookkeeping of the Kodaira–Spencer / Legendre-twist phenomenon at level 2. The explicit μ_4 ∧ ω_J obstruction is a nice detail, but the underlying mathematics is standard and would not surprise a specialist.

'μ_4^×' near the bottom should match the earlier μ_4^♮ (or μ_4^*) notation.
'Une fois [?]' should read 'Une fois α fixé'.
The dangling 'μ_2-torseurs' after 'et on voit' belongs to the sentence 'forment ... les sections d'un μ_2-torseur L_α(E)'.
